atAGlance: Cháo lòng is pork offal rice porridge with ginger, herbs, pepper, and soft rice. It is warming and traditional, but more adventurous than chicken porridge.
whatItIs: Cháo lòng is rice porridge with pork offal, ginger, scallions, herbs, and pepper. It is soft and warming, but the toppings are more adventurous than chicken porridge.
howToEnjoy: Add pepper, herbs, and ginger to brighten the bowl. Choose cháo gà if you want gentle porridge without offal.
howLocalsOrder: Cháo lòng is a comfort-bowl order, especially good when you want something soft. Ask for extra ginger or less pepper before mixing, and order fried dough on the side if the shop has it.
worthKnowing: Lòng means offal. This is a useful word to recognize if organ meats are a yes or no for you. In Vietnam, cháo is a rice-porridge comfort-food lane. The topping tells you whether the bowl stays gentle or turns more adventurous.
goodToKnow: Lòng means offal or organs. If you want the gentle porridge experience without organs, choose cháo gà.

orderLine.vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô cháo lòng.
